perspective:
**Keith Ndiaye’s available information:**

- He and Elizabeth are colleagues at a construction company: Keith is a construction worker, Elizabeth is the receptionist. They have a friendly but professional relationship, usually interacting when Keith visits the office for paperwork or project updates.
- Recently, over the past few days, Keith noticed Elizabeth was unusually curt/short with him.
- He wondered whether he had upset her through a misunderstanding or an unknowing mistake.
- He asked Elizabeth if he had done something to upset her. He heard her say no, that she was dealing with personal stuff, and she apologized if she seemed short.
- After this, Keith felt sympathetic and wanted to offer support.
- He told Elizabeth he understood she was going through a tough time, offered to listen, and suggested a coffee break. He heard her accept and thank him.
- During the coffee break, Elizabeth shared more about her personal stresses. Keith perceived them as quite severe.
- Keith suggested Elizabeth consider talking to a professional, saying an external perspective can help. He heard her say she had thought about it but was not sure and felt hesitant about seeking help.
- Afterward, Keith noticed Elizabeth become slightly withdrawn. He believed his suggestion might have embarrassed her and felt regretful.
- He told her he hoped he hadn’t overstepped, and that he wanted her to know he was there to support her. He heard her say he hadn’t overstepped, that she appreciated his concern, and that it was a lot to think about.
- Following their last conversation, Keith observed that Elizabeth seemed more open and appreciative of his concern. He believes she values his support and feels more comfortable around him now.
- He intends to maintain this supportive relationship.
- He told Elizabeth he was glad they talked and that he is always available if she needs to chat or take a break together. He heard her thank him, say it means a lot, and say she feels better knowing she has his support.

Keith does not have access to Elizabeth’s private thoughts, unspoken feelings, or any details about her stress beyond what she told him and what he observed.
